entities.summary:
United States of America is a sovereign nation in Northern America, Americas. Its capital is Washington, D.C.. Official languages include None at federal level (English de facto). Government: Federal presidential constitutional republic. Population: approximately 342.5 million. Area: 9,833,520 km². Comprehensive index for the United States covering indigenous civilizations (Cahokia, Ancestral Puebloans, etc.), European colonization (Jamestown 1607, Plymouth 1620, 13 colonies), independence 1776 (Revolutionary War), Constitution 1787, Westward expansion/Manifest Destiny, slavery (institution/abolitionism), Civil War 1861-65 (~750,000 dead, ended slavery), Reconstruction/Jim Crow, Industrial Revolution, Gilded Age, Progressive Era, WWI entry 1917, Great Depression 1929, New Deal, WWII 1941-45 (superpower emergence), Cold War 1947-91 (USSR rivalry, containment, nuclear arms race, proxy wars), Civil Rights Movement (Brown v.

Board, MLK, Civil Rights Acts 1964/65), Vietnam War, Watergate, Reagan conservatism, 9/11 2001, War on Terror (Afghanistan/Iraq), 2008 financial crisis, Obama first Black president, Trump populism, January 6 2021 Capitol attack, Biden, and global hegemony.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The United States of America played a pivotal role in shaping modern democracy, with its Constitution and Bill of Rights influencing global human rights standards. The country's westward expansion and industrialization transformed the continent, while its involvement in two world wars had far-reaching consequences for international relations.
